query_title: Feature Request: Workspace-specific keybindings.json
query_body:
I am preparing to lead a workshop where I will be using VSCode as the suggested code editor. I've been able to bundle some useful settings, extensions and tasks directly for the class via the .vscode directory. Unfortunately, there is no way to bundle suggested keybindings for my project in the same way.

Technically, it seems relatively straightforward: the json format is already specified and keybindingResolver.ts is already wired up to take in the fixed native mappings and override them with the user-specific keybindings. This could either be extended to take two sets of overrides, or the workspace-specific ones could be concatenated to the user-specific override list.

Rather, I think the biggest problem is a matter of determining what .vscode/keybindings.json should do. Personally, I'd like to just use any keybindings found in that file first, then defer to user settings, then defer to native (just like the other .vscode config files), but before I consider working on a PR, I'd like to get some more opinions on what people think about this idea.

target_title: Closing the last open file, then hiding and showing the explorer reopens the file
target_body:
- VSCode Version: 1.31.0
- OS Version: Linux x86 (Solus)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Close all open files
2. Open a file or two from the explorer
3. Close the files (they remain selected in the explorer)
4. Hide the explorer (either click on the explorer icon, CTRL+B, or switch to searching, extensions, etc.)
5. Show the explorer
6. The most recently closed file is now opened

This behavior has changed from the previous release. In the previous release, the file was deselected from the explorer when it was closed. In 1.31.0, the file remains selected, which gives the behavior described above.

I prefer the previous behavior, as usually, I don't want to reopen the most recently closed file. It causes extra visual noise.

Some examples of past related issues are: https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode/issues/998 and https://github.com/Microsoft/vscode/issues/6922


Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

![Example of behavior](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7329219/52428262-9bae5080-2acf-11e9-8dad-838d77936996.gif)
label: VALID
reason: Both describe the same root bug: a closed file stays selected in Explorer and reopens when the sidebar regains focus/visibility.

----

Edit by @aeschli (VSCode team):

What you see is the new semantic highlighting feature updating the highlighting with resolved information from the TypeScript server. The server takes a while to load, depending on the size of the project, that's why the highlighting comes in delayed.

As a result, each identifier gets colored & styled with the color of the symbol it resolves to. You can see this the easiest in the imports where you can now see what is a function, variable or type. Another example are that readonly variables ('consts') and members can get a different style that modifiable variables, if the theme has defined different colors & styles.

There are still bugs with the way symbols are classified (e.g. [INLINE_CODE] and other symbols that are both function and object), but the color changes as such are intended.

We're still debating what the best default setting for semantic highlighting is as many see the updated colors as a bug.

You can turn the semantic highlighting feature off with
[INLINE_CODE]

I created https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Semantic-Highlighting-Overview#semantic-highlighting with the planed changes for this weeks stable fix release (1.43.1):
We will only enable semantic highlighting by default for the built-in themes. Other themes can opt-in (or it can be enabled in the user settings).

query_title: Proposal: Headless services
query_body:
Related to #1437, though this isn't the only solution to it.

A number of forms of discovery/naming/addressing are covered by other issues:
- IP-per-service (#1107)
- DNS for services (#1261, #146)
- Externally visible services (#1161)
- External services (#2358)
- Nominal services for fixed-replicated (i.e., not dynamically scaled) services and singletons (#260)
- Master-elected services (#1542)
- Sharded services (#1064)

The remaining hole is individually addressable dynamically scaled services and worker pools.

The user could tie use PreStart/PostStart and PreStop hooks to self-register with a discovery system, such as etcd, consul, or eureka, as mentioned in #386 and elsewhere.

A more integrated solution could be to support _Headless services_. The endpoints_controller already creates endpoint records in etcd for services, which are also made available via the API. Headless services would do the same, just without creating an IP and/or DNS name for the service. This would create an API that clients could use to watch the set of endpoints associated with the headless service, and which would take advantage of whatever UI, readiness probes, etc. we add for services more generally, and which would be available for Kubernetes applications without the need to run a separate discovery service. 

The tradeoff for a developer would be whether to couple to the Kubernetes API or to a particular discovery system. This API would not preclude the self-registration approach, however, and adapters for other discovery systems could be built upon this API, as well.

Improvements to the existing endpoints API and implementation (e.g. efficient watching of joins/leaves) are orthogonal issues.

target_title: Document why we don't use maps in the API in api-conventions.md
target_body:
Forked from #1980.

The API has a number of lists containing names embedded in objects, such as Volumes, Containers, Ports, Env, and VolumeMounts. Both configuration and field references (e.g., in filter expressions, events) are uglier and/or more verbose when using lists rather than maps. This puts us at a disadvantage compared to other systems with more elegant API and/or configuration schemas (e.g., Fig).

Automatically translating maps into lists of named objects appears to be hard. In JSON and YAML, structures and maps cannot be distinguished without a schema. It looks like we'd need either duplicate fields, duplicate schemas, or a custom parser in order to support both formats in the same API version. Duplicate schemas have proven hard to maintain, both in Kubernetes and internally. I don't think we want to maintain parallel API versions forever, either. The go-yaml parser is around 9k lines of code -- a custom parser is not something we want to own, IMO. 

The specific proposal here is to:
- change these lists to maps
- make these name fields optional and auto-populate them from map keys in apiserver, so that names are available in subobjects even without the maps to which they belong

Port name is currently optional. It would effectively be required. A convention of "p<port number>" would be straightforward for users/tools, however, such as in the case of ports auto-populated from Docker images (e.g., by podex).

This would be a breaking change. We could do it in v1beta3.

The names of top-level objects, in ObjectMeta in v1beta3, would not be changed. Those can be auto-populated in v1beta3 by clients in a straightforward manner.

query_title: Document API/system design principles and patterns
query_body:
Related to #5476, #2003, #1007, #5620, and other issues.

The PR creation rate and number of contributors are both growing. In order to scale the effort, we need to better document the patterns we want additions to the system and API to follow, so that we can better parallelize the design and review effort. I'm filing this issue to solicit important principles and patterns to document. I volunteer to create the actual document and/or presentation slides.

What do you think isn't sufficiently covered by existing design docs and/or isn't sufficiently discoverable? What principles/patterns do you find yourself explaining over and over again? What properties would you be unhappy to have violated/degraded/changed by new PRs? 

I'm thinking more about reasonably general issues rather than implementation-oriented invariants that apply to very specific/narrow parts of the code. 

Examples (some areas, some principles):
- Declarative APIs, desired state and current state
- Level-based operation: Functionality must be level-based, meaning the system must operate correctly given the desired state and the current/observed state, regardless of how many intermediate state updates may have been missed. Edge-based behavior must be just an optimization.
- Status must be 100% reconstructable by observation. Any history kept must be just an optimization and not required for correct operation.
- Phase, Reason, Message, Conditions, etc. vs. a single state machine with lots of states
- Composable, a la carte functionality
- Transparent, no glass to break
- More generally, [Eric Raymond's 17 UNIX rules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_philosophy#Eric_Raymond.E2.80.99s_17_Unix_Rules)
- Only the apiserver should communicate with etcd/store, and not other components (scheduler, kubelet, etc.)

target_title: 'int' in API types considered harmful
target_body:
The go compiler is allowed to treat 'int' as either 32 or 64 bits. This is unacceptable for an API that may need to work on multiple systems, with binaries compiled by compilers with different ideas about the proper bit width for an int. Therefore, we need to use int64 or int32 in our API objects, not int.

For cases where a small amount of static data is desired. This could include
1. configuration for containers whose process is configured by files
2. small-medium amounts of static data, such as an archive of www data for a static site server

query_title: Support transferables in webview postMessage
query_body:
Issue asking _what_ is supported: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/79257

[INLINE_CODE] does not support transferables (eg. typed arrays) so [INLINE_CODE] for example ends up being encoded as an object like [INLINE_CODE]. Some approaches I've tried to workaround this problem:

- Convert the typed array to an array [INLINE_CODE], this is slow, duplicates memory and causes unnecessary GC
- "Encode" the typed array as an ascii string and "decode" it back on the other side, this is slower but ends up being a smaller payload that [INLINE_CODE], benefits also don't seem to kick in until the payload is quite large

The real fix here is just supporting transferring typed arrays.

I'm not sure if it's possible but it would be amazing if we could use [INLINE_CODE]s between the ext host and webview, then there is no transfer time. For example the ext host could initialize the SAB and transfer it over for use, if the webview needed a bigger buffer it could request it via [INLINE_CODE].
target_title: Document what types webview.postMessage supports
target_body:
The setup is as follows: We have a a web view extension to which we post messages. We would like to read a file in the workspace and send that file's data to the extension using the [INLINE_CODE] API. 

Unfortunately, all attempts to post a message that is not a string have resulted in the receiver getting nothing. If I convert the file data to base64 I can send it successfully. The files we are using are on the order of 10mb. Not huge, but not super quick to convert to base64 and then back to a Blob on the receiving end.

One excellent solution would be to support [Transferable Objects](https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2011/12/Transferable-Objects-Lightning-Fast). I suspect that the [INLINE_CODE] API is doing something to disallow this, perhaps for security reasons, but it'd be really useful.

Thanks!

query_title: Refine error on line audio cue
query_body:
Screen reader users navigate through an editor via the arrow keys/mouse and are informed of errors with an audio cue when:

1. the cursor lands on a line with an error via line change
3. the cursor lands in an error range via a column change

When a screen reader user goes to a new line with an error, they hear the audio cue, but aren't advised as to whether or not the column they've landed on contains an error. 

In order to know this, they must explore the characters on that line. 

While working on the fix for https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/174857, @kieferrm suggested it could be advantageous to have separate audio cues for each context. That would fix this case. 

Here's what I propose:

Separate audio cues for:
1. the cursor lands within an error range via line and/or column change
2. the cursor lands on a line with an error outside of the error range via line change

any thoughts are appreciated: @isidorn and @jooyoungseo

target_title: Provide legacy server when remote requirements fail
target_body:
<details>
<summary>Following options were considered,</summary>

1) Build Node.js with [--fully-static](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/68885d512640556ba95b18f5ab2e0b9e76013399/configure.py#L156-L161) option 
 - No versioning issue from glibc and libstdc++
 - Symbols are not exported which means native modules (which are dynamic libraries) cannot be loaded

2) Build Node.js with [--partly-static](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/68885d512640556ba95b18f5ab2e0b9e76013399/configure.py#L163-L168) option
 - glibc is still dynamic so versioning issue persists
 - with native modules this mode will be a footgun

3) Using alpine binaries as fallback
 - musl is dynamically linked in both core native modules as well as executable, which means it cannot be loaded in glibc platforms

4) Shipping glibc, libstdc++ dynamic libraries as part of the server package
 - We would need to change the executable rpath to load these libraries which would then be picked up by any other dynamic libraries that get loaded into the executable (applies to native node modules). Will work for all cases
 - Downside is we are now committing to track cve fixes in both these libraries
</details>

**Legacy Server:**

We have pre-requisite checks for both [exec server path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/cli/src/util/prereqs.rs) as well as the [normal remote connection path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/resources/server/bin/helpers/check-requirements-linux.sh). Idea is that when the checks fail we will download what we call [INLINE_CODE] on these machines and everything else should work as expected,

- Server and core node modules are built using sysroot containing glibc 2.17 and gcc 7
- Downgrades the minimum requirements to GLIBC >= 2.17 and GLI
